cybersecurity.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution

Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell.

For five of them, its maintainers say, proof-of-concept exploits, or PoCs, have shown that crafted input can run code on the machine. "We are aware of PoCs that prove some of them can be used to trigger remote code execution," the maintainers said.

The decade-old flaw, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed "nginx2root," has been present in NGINX's open-source code since version 1.9.5, released on September 22, 2015. Fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 came out today.
